{"id":"mimid-96tt","title":"spec: say where a MIMI-backed VTC call's media keys come from, which no draft does","description":"The substantive opportunity from the 2026-11-23 reading, and the one
piece nobody has specified anywhere. Needs Mark's approval to write,
being a jmap-chat-spec change.

THE TWO HALVES THAT ALREADY FIT:

- OUR SIDE declines to say. draft-atwood-jmap-vtc-00's `e2eeEnabled` is
  a state signal only: "The mechanism (WebRTC Encoded Transform, SFrame,
  or other) is media-layer-defined; this field is the state signal for
  client UI (e.g., displaying a lock icon)." Deliberate, and right for a
  standalone VTC capability. It also already has the binding: a
  VTCCall may carry `chatId`, and §Optional Binding Fields makes it
  present when the chat capability is on the account.
- MIMI'S SIDE HAS THE MECHANISM AND NO POLICY.
  draft-ietf-mls-extensions-11 §4.4 gives a forward-secure
  SafeExportSecret(ComponentID) per app component, §4.1 makes a
  ComponentID application-scoped, and mimi-protocol-07 §10.2 and §10.3
  show MIMI assigning its own app components (franking_agent,
  participant_list). No media component is registered, and
  mimi-content §5.10 puts calling out of scope.

SO THE SENTENCE THAT IS MISSING, AND THAT WE ARE PLACED TO WRITE: when a
VTC call is bound by `chatId` to a Chat that is bound to a MIMI room,
the call's media keys are derived from that room's MLS group with the
safe exporter, under a named component. That turns `e2eeEnabled` from a
UI lamp into something a second implementation can reproduce, and it
costs the VTC draft nothing, because the binding is already optional.

WHAT IT NEEDS, and each is a real question rather than boilerplate:
- A component id. MIMI has not assigned one and we cannot. Follow the
  repo's existing practice for unassigned code points -- a provisional
  value marked INVENTED, NOT FROM SPEC, as mimid-1wgh.4.81.18 does for
  the did:webvh credential type -- and say plainly it is provisional.
- Which secret feeds what. One exported secret per epoch per component,
  then the media layer's own derivation (SFrame has its own key
  schedule). Say where our responsibility stops.
- Rekeying on epoch change. An MLS commit changes the epoch, so the
  exported secret changes; a call in progress has to roll media keys or
  pin an epoch. This is the hard part and the draft should state a rule
  rather than leave it.
- Who is entitled. The MLS group is the room's membership, and a call is
  a subset; §4.4 gives one secret to the whole group, so a call keyed
  that way is readable by every room member, not only the participants.
  That may be acceptable for a call room whose membership IS the call
  (room-policy §5's parent-dependent shape), and is not acceptable for
  a call among three people in a twenty-person room. Mark's call, and it
  probably decides whether a call needs its own room.

That last point is the one that makes this worth doing properly rather
than quickly: it links the keying question to room-policy's call-room
model, and it is the argument for implementing bead mimid-1wgh.108.

ORDER: this comes after mimid-bcji (the plain session-part mapping, which
is just writing down what the code does), and it is worth having a view
on before posting the WG issue on mimid-1wgh.37.106, since the WG may
ask what we would do.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-11-23T18:56:22.704519058Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-11-23T18:56:22.704519058Z","labels":["human"]}

{"design":"WORKED THROUGH 2026-11-23. A recommendation, for Mark to accept or
reject before anything is written into a draft.

THE QUESTION: where does a MIMI-backed call's media keys come from, and
who can compute them.

THE CRUX, which decides everything else: mls-extensions §4.4's
SafeExportSecret(ComponentID) is derived from the epoch secret, so EVERY
GROUP MEMBER CAN COMPUTE IT. The signature takes a ComponentID and
nothing else -- no per-call context -- so a component gets one secret
per epoch and any further derivation is equally computable by every
member. Entitlement therefore cannot be fixed by derivation. A call
among three people in a twenty-person room, keyed from the room's
exporter, is readable by all twenty if they can get the ciphertext from
the SFU or the network. That is a confidentiality failure against the
plain product expectation.

So the group has to BE the entitled set, or the keys must not come from
the group secret at all. mls-extensions gives one mechanism for each:

- §4.4 Exported Secrets: one forward-secure secret per component,
  computable by the whole group.
- §4.2 Safe HPKE: SafeEncryptWithLabel(PublicKey, ComponentID, Label,
  Context, Plaintext) lets a component encrypt to any HPKE key pair MLS
  generated, which includes an individual member's leaf key.

RECOMMENDATION: TWO CASES, AND PREFER THE FIRST.

CASE 1, the recommended shape: the call gets its own room, and its
media keys come from §4.4's exporter under a MIMI media component.

This is exactly room-policy §5's call room -- fixed_membership plus
parent_dependent, "for example, for room used for a multi-media call of
clients in a Group DM" -- and working the keying out shows that note is
not incidental. It is the answer. MLS key material is group-scoped, so
making the call its own group makes entitlement STRUCTURAL rather than a
matter of cryptographic bookkeeping.

What falls out for free, and this is the strongest argument:
- Removing someone from the call is an MLS Remove. That changes the
  epoch, which changes the exported secret, so they lose media access
  immediately and cannot decrypt anything after it. Forward secrecy for
  the call, with no media-layer rekey protocol to specify.
- Adding someone is a Commit, which rekeys the same way, so a late
  joiner cannot decrypt earlier media either.
- The call has its own membership list, its own lifetime and its own
  participant roles, all of which MLS and room policy already handle.
- Epoch change is the natural rekey signal, so "when do media keys
  roll" needs no new answer.

CASE 2, for an ad-hoc call among a subset of a room without making one:
the initiator mints a call key and distributes it with §4.2's Safe HPKE,
encrypted to each participant's leaf HPKE public key under the media
component. The sender has the leaf keys already, from the ratchet tree.

Its cost is the reason to prefer Case 1: removing a participant
mid-call means minting a new key and redistributing to the remaining
set, which is a media-layer rekey protocol we would have to design and
specify. Case 1 gets that from MLS.

THE OTHER THREE QUESTIONS, now easy:
- Component id: no media component is registered and we cannot register
  one. Use a provisional value marked INVENTED, NOT FROM SPEC, as
  mimid-1wgh.4.81.18 does for the did:webvh code points, and say in the
  draft that it is provisional.
- Where our responsibility stops: we provide one secret per epoch per
  component, of a stated length. The media layer runs its own key
  schedule from it; SFrame has one. The draft says that and no more.
- Rekeying: in Case 1 there is nothing to specify, because the epoch is
  the rekey. Say that explicitly, since it is the payoff.

WHAT THIS IMPLIES, and it is a real consequence rather than a tidy one:

Bead mimid-1wgh.108 (parent-dependent rooms, parsed but not
implemented) stops being a P3 nice-to-have and becomes the prerequisite
for keyed calls. And ietf-wg-mimi/mimi-room-policy#40 matters more than
it looked: the strict-subset rule forbids a call whose participants are
everyone in the Group DM, which is the commonest call there is, so Case
1 cannot be implemented as the draft is written. That is now the
strongest reason for the WG to answer #40.

NOT WRITTEN INTO ANY DRAFT YET. If Mark accepts this, the order is: say
it in draft-atwood-jmap-chat-mimi-00's §Calls, which already ends with
"A later revision may say what a call bound to a MIMI room derives its
media keys from"; then the WG issue (mimid-1wgh.37.106) can say what we
did rather than only asking."}
